candidates.text:
No, I won’t check out your portfolio.

Here’s why.

Anytime you ask someone to do something, it’s a pitch. In a pitch, say what’s in it for the other person.

What’s in it for me to check out your portfolio? Why would I spend my time, energy, and attention—all of which I value highly—on that as opposed to anywhere else?

If there’s nothing in it for me, then you’re asking for charity.

If you’re asking for charity, then ask for charity. Make it clear. I like doing favors sometimes and being charitable sometimes. But I can’t tell if that’s what you’re asking for, and I won’t assume it.

Even if I agreed to it, you haven’t even given me any criteria. Is there something specific you want help with? Something to improve? Something you’re stuck on? Some job it’s not doing?

General questions get general answers. Specific questions get specific answers.

Since I don’t know what you want help with and there doesn’t seem to be much incentive for me, it’s a pass.

Here are some examples of pitches I would consider more (even if I’d still say no):

“Dan, would you be willing to do me a favor and review my portfolio to help me land a design job working on a U.S.-based team for a fintech startup?”

“Dan, can you please review my portfolio to see if the UI design work feels closer to junior or senior caliber? I’ll make a donation to your favorite non-profit as a token of thanks.”

“Dan, would you mind looking at my portfolio to see if I’m the kind of person you’d hire? I know you value your time, attention, and energy, so I’d gladly take any feedback you can provide after looking for even 30 seconds.”

@odeniransulaimo, wanna pitch again? I’m open to you trying again if you’d like.

But even better: pitch someone who’s in a closer position to help you get what you want. If you want a job at a sports betting startup, pitch a hiring manager at a sports betting startup to check out your portfolio. Even if they won’t hire you for THEIR startup, their feedback would be way more relevant to getting a job at a sports betting startup than my feedback would be, since I’ve never worked at a sport betting startup.

In short, when you pitch, make it about them and make it as easy as possible for them to give you what you want.

I built a Grok Bot @bot @grok because Zillow filters can’t do what real estate searches need.

Listing sites want a single number like “2 beds, 1.5 baths.” But real people have rules like:

- 1 bed only if it has 1.5+ baths, otherwise 2 bed 2 bath. 

- Walk to the beach proximity increases budget up to $1,000 more.

- Community pool OR freestanding bathtub in bathroom. 

Just as important, many listing features are only found in photos!! Carpet in the bathroom isn’t in the listing text, its in photo number 15 if you look closely.

And filtering “15 min commute” isn’t enough. Real people need to know Wednesday at 5:40pm with traffic and what the 2AM crime reality is for that block. 

Haus Hunter is a personal housing investigator. It keeps the search going against rules like those so you’re not clicking through hundreds of duds.
